decisions.executionNote: Raise the left arm into an elbow-up approach toward the left tube; begin matching its diagonal axis. Right arm stays home.
Continue the elevated left approach and rotate toward a downward grasp aligned with the tube; preserve elbow-up continuity.
Bring the open left gripper above the tube midpoint and finish aligning the downward approach; stop above grasp height for visual refinement.
Refine the left tube alignment, descend to body-grasp height, and close. Retention will be checked visually during lifting.
Lift the closed left gripper clear of the table with a small backward retreat; inspect whether the tube follows.
The tube follows the left gripper. Rotate it gradually upright while moving toward the rack's left front large slot, keeping it elevated.
Finish rotating the retained tube upright above the left slot. Lower only to a clear pre-insertion height for alignment checking.
Make a small right/forward correction over the left front large hole, then lower the upright tube toward insertion depth with the grip closed.
Seat the first tube another 25 mm into the aligned left slot, pause, then open the gripper to release it.
Withdraw the open left gripper to check the released tube, while starting an elevated right-arm approach to the nearer right tube.
The first tube did not remain upright; clear the left arm for a better view and later recovery. Continue the right arm's open approach above its tube.
Return the empty left arm toward home. Position the right gripper above the near right tube, using the latest visible cap-to-tip diagonal.
Center the right gripper on the near tube body, remove remaining approach tilt, descend to grasp height, and close.
Lift the near right tube with the grip closed and check that it stays between the fingers before transport.
Transport the retained right tube inward at clearance height while gradually rotating it upright. Keep the left arm clear.
Continue the right tube's elevated inward transfer and upright rotation, avoiding the rack until alignment is visible.
Finish upright rotation above the right front rack slot. Maintain closed grip and pause high to check alignment.
Lower the upright right tube to a closer alignment view, correcting slightly inward and forward over the rightmost large slot.
Insert the aligned right tube vertically another 45 mm without releasing yet; check the tube and slot at depth.
The tube appears to have slid upward against the rack rather than seated. Lift slightly and shift right/forward to center its tip over the large opening before retrying.
Try a short controlled vertical insertion at the corrected hole alignment, keeping the grip closed and checking for further sliding.
Lower the tube the final short distance into the opening and release without lateral motion; verify it remains supported by the rack.
Clear the open right gripper upward and backward from the rack to remove finger contact and inspect whether the tube is supported.
Leave the released tube supported in the rack and clear upward toward the remaining right tube, gradually changing to a downward grasp.
Replan after the continuity guard using slower lift and rotation increments, remaining clear of the released tube.
Approach the remaining loose right tube from above, rotating the open gripper to its diagonal axis with conservative continuous motion.
Complete the downward, tube-aligned approach above the loose right tube, stopping at clearance for wrist-view centering.
Adjust the grasp toward the cap while descending partway, aiming for a higher body grasp that leaves more tube length below the fingers.
Finish a higher-body grasp near the cap, slightly matching the tube's table tilt, then close while stationary.
Lift the higher grasp clear of the table and retreat slightly with the right gripper closed; verify the tube follows before turning upright.
The high grasp is retaining the tube. Begin an elevated, gradual upright rotation toward an unoccupied central rack slot.
Continue the slow elevated transfer toward the central opening while turning the retained tube upright.
Finish the rotation above the rack center at safe height, then inspect the actual retained tube axis before descending.
The tube is tilted within the high grasp. Compensate by pitching the right wrist while raising the EE to preserve clearance, then inspect the tube axis from the head view.
With the tube's tilt compensated, bring its tip toward the central front opening using a small inward correction and a controlled 40 mm descent.
Lower the compensated tube vertically another 30 mm while holding it, watching whether its tip enters the central opening without slipping.
Continue the slow vertical seating motion while the cap remains fixed in the grasp; inspect depth before releasing.
Release the high-grasp tube at the current seating depth without lateral motion, then let it settle before withdrawing.
Withdraw the open right gripper upward and back to verify the released central tube remains in the slot without finger support.
The central tube remains upright in its slot. Clear outward and begin a downward approach to recover the leaning tube on the rack's right side.
Position the open gripper above the leaning tube's cap for a recovery grasp, keeping clear of the upright central tube.
After the guard, use only a short downward correction at the observed orientation and close around the recovered tube near its cap; check retention before moving.
The recovery grasp missed and the tube tilted left. Open, lift clear, and approach its newly visible cap from above without disturbing the central upright tube.
Back the right arm out of the tightly folded recovery approach with small continuous steps. Begin an elevated left-arm approach to the loose left tube; keep both grippers open.
The prior chunk executed nothing. Reduce the right escape motion to quarter-sized increments while starting the left arm's elbow-up lift.
Move the left arm toward the loose tube while gradually aligning with its reversed cap direction. Return the empty right arm outward and back, away from the rack.
Continue the left elevated approach to the loose tube's cap end while bringing the empty right arm back through its own workspace.
Finish matching the left tube's reversed axis above its cap end. Bring the empty right arm nearly home while preserving both elbow-up branches.
Replan from the guard stop with smaller right-arm return increments. Finish centering the open left gripper above the loose tube's cap-end body.
Use the wrist view to shift the left grasp onto the tube's cap-end body while descending, then close; keep the right arm clear at home.
Lift the left cap-end grasp clear of the table with the grip closed, moving slightly outward and back to keep wrist configuration continuous.
The left tube is retained. Begin a slow upright rotation that unwinds the wrist while raising for clearance and staying in the left workspace.
Continue unwinding and turning the retained left tube upright at clearance height, with only a small forward translation.
